questions.prompt: A heater runs at 12 V and 4.0 A for 5 minutes. How much energy does it transfer?
questions.explanation: E = V × I × t = 12 × 4.0 × 300 = 14 400 J. Remember t in seconds.

questions.prompt: 27 000 J warms a 1.0 kg metal block from 20 °C to 50 °C. What is the specific heat capacity of the metal?
A student's value of c is higher than the true value. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Energy was lost to the surroundings, so the temperature rise was too small
The block was heated for too short a time

questions.explanation: Not all of E heated the block. A smaller Δθ in c = E/(mΔθ) gives a bigger c.

questions.prompt: A drop of oil in the thermometer hole improves thermal contact, so the thermometer reads closer to the block's real temperature.
questions.explanation: Air is a poor conductor; oil fills the gap.

steps.text: Put the heater and thermometer (with oil) in the block and wrap it in insulation
Switch on, read the voltmeter and ammeter, and start the stopwatch
Record the temperature every minute for 10 minutes, then switch off

questions.explanation: Set up first, then the start temperature before any heating, then time the heating and record regularly.

questions.prompt: Water has a specific heat capacity of 4200 J/kg°C; aluminium about 900 J/kg°C. The same heater warms 1 kg of each. Which warms up faster?
questions.explanation: Aluminium needs less energy per kilogram for each degree, so its temperature rises faster.
